utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. I see that in the Defence team Mr. Stewart is not present at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Mr. Stewart will not be here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And on the Prosecution's team, I see you, Mr. Tieger, Mr. Resch, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will be assisted today by Mr. Charles Curilan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. May I take it that the Prosecution is ready to continue examination-in-chief of Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are. I'd like to raise one preliminary matter before we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that is with respect to Mr. Hasanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It turns out that Mr. Hasanovic will not be able to secure his travel documents in sufficient time to be here this week. We have advised the Defence this morning of that development and wanted to alert the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As I indicated before, it seems that it's not Mr. Hasanovic who doesn't want to appear, but it's rather documents he would need. Whenever the Prosecution, and I repeat that, would need the assistance of the Chamber to see whether this problem could be solved, the Chamber is ready to hear whatever you would ask us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We're grateful, Your Honour. Just to clarify: I believe that -- it seems apparent that he will be able to obtain the documents. It's just not in sufficient time. We expect him to have them by the end of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any further issues? If not, Mr. Usher, may I ask you to escort Mr. Treanor into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your examination will be continued, but before I give an opportunity to Mr. Tieger to proceed, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've made at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, at the conclusion of Friday's session, we played for the Court clip 2 of an intercept dated 28 July 1991, and we deferred your comments on that clip until today, because you indicated it required some contextualisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I might add for the Court's benefit that that particular intercept is to be found, or at least the English translation of that intercept is to be found at tab 6 in the intercept binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if I could ask you now for your comments on that portion of the intercept.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wonder if it would be a good idea to play it again to refresh everyone's memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, we can do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps that's not a bad idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We're ready to start whenever the booth is ready and we have sound. [Intercept played](no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could move to the second clip, please. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's certainly a lot in that second clip. One thing that emerges in there which came out in the first clip as well is the idea that the SDS would like to keep the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina within Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Yugoslavia, and on the one hand, Dr. Karadzic tries to restrain some of Mr. Brdjanin's enthusiasm for regionalisation in order to make sure that Mr. Brdjanin keeps his eye on the ball, so to speak, that is, on the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina. On the other hand, in discussions with the Muslim leadership, he's indicating that if they won't agree to that, to keeping the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina within Yugoslavia, then they, the SDS leadership, has a response to that planned and seems to be assuring Mr. Brdjanin that that's -- they know what they're doing and they have things planned out. Now, I'd like to add to that, which is why I didn't want to get into this Friday afternoon, that the occasion for Mr. Brdjanin's phone call, as indicated at the beginning of that conversation, and as indicated at the beginning of that second clip, which might have been a bit obscure to listeners coming in at that point, is that Mr. Brdjanin is disturbed by something that Mr. Simovic said. Mr. Simovic, as I mentioned earlier, was the highest-ranking SDS designated member of the government of BH, to the effect that there would be no regionalisation, which of course is not Mr. Brdjanin's understanding of the situation. Mr. Karadzic indicates to him that, you know, the negotiation is going on and you probably said it for that reason, and anyways don't worry too much about him because he is not in the party. He is not a party leader; he's a government leader. Now, what was happening at that time, about this time - and the date of this conversation again is the 28th of July - is that negotiations or discussions were under way or about to get under way between the SDS leadership and Muslim leaders on the future of BH within Yugoslavia. These negotiations are a bit obscure to me. We don't have much documentation directly relating to them, although I think there are one or two documents that we'll see very shortly which refer to them. On the one hand, there seem to have been more or less continuous contacts with the leadership of the SDA, in particular, Mr. Izetbegovic. On the other hand, at precisely this time, the SDS leadership was engaged with contacts with the leadership of the Muslim Bosniak organisation, which was another Bosnian Muslim political party. They only had two seats in the Assembly of BH, were not a very powerful party, therefore; however, they were a Muslim party. And in fact, on the 30th of July, there was a meeting or a press conference in Belgrade, featuring Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Adil Zulfikarpasic, who was the leader of the MBO, the Muslim Bosniak Organisation, with a view to an agreement between those two organisations. Those discussions apparently continued and, as I say, I think we're going to see some more documents relating to that. One of the things that apparently the MBO was against, as was the SDA, was regionalisation. So that was kind of -- was going to be a topic of conversation during those discussions, and I can only suppose that Dr. Karadzic didn't want at that time to come out too firmly, publicly, in favour of regionalisation, which is something that they were going to be negotiating with Muslim leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next document is found at tab 31 of binder 2. And it refers to a meeting of 12 August 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, that document is now on the screen as well, with the first paragraph highlighted. Can you tell us about that meeting and who was in attendance, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This meeting took place in Belgrade on the 12th of August, 1991, pursuant to an invitation issued by Slobodan Milosevic, as president of Serbia, to representatives of, of course his own republic, but also representatives of Montenegro and Bosnia and Herzegovina, to attend talks in Belgrade about the future of Yugoslavia, in particular, a future Yugoslavia which might only include those three republics. This is an idea which became known as the Belgrade Initiative. In the first paragraph here, we can see a list of the attendees. As the Court will notice, Montenegro and Serbia are represented by the presidents of their respective assemblies as well as members of the Presidencies. Bosnia-Herzegovina, on the other hand, is only represented by Mr. Krajisnik as President of the Assembly. Now, the invitation had gone out to Mr. Izetbegovic as well. He refused to attend, and the whole issue of this meeting and who attended and who didn't attend got to be the subject of recriminations within Bosnia and Herzegovina, why didn't Mr. Izetbegovic go, why did Mr. Krajisnik go, that sort of thing. I don't think that need detain us too much here. I think we can perhaps move on in the document. I would call attention, if we could, to the fourth paragraph, which is not highlighted, which says: "The participants of the Belgrade meeting unanimously held the historic agreement between the Muslims and Serbs in BH, emphasising that the agreement was a big step towards a peaceful solution to the crisis, an affirmation of the equality of the Yugoslav peoples." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Now, this so-called agreement between the Muslims and Serbs in BH was one of the main conditions for the success of this whole initiative. The most important thing I think for the Court to know about that agreement is it in fact never took place, that is, the negotiations with the MBO did not result in such an agreement, nor did any talks with the SDA. Q.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The next selection, Your Honours, can be found in the intercept binder at tab 7. That is an intercept dated 13 August 1991. And if we could have that played, please. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, your comments, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this intercept we move a little bit from high politics to more day-to-day affairs. This conversation is an example of the types of consultations that took place between Mr. Karadzic and the SDS-designated members of the Presidency and the government on day-to-day problems. In this particular case, Mrs. Plavsic is concerned about the situation where apparently Albanian volunteers to fight on behalf of the Republic of Croatia and Croatia are passing through Banja Luka and causing concern among the Serbs there, and he -- Dr. Karadzic advises her on how to handle the situation. He mentions the local SDS people in Banja Luka, not only Mr. Radic, who is identified as the president of the Assembly in Banja Luka, but also Stojan Zupljanin, who is the head of the Ministry of Internal Affairs Security Services Centre in Banja Luka and was an SDS designee. Mrs. Plavsic seems to think it needs a little more attention from Sarajevo end of things, and so Dr. Karadzic encourages her to call the SDS people in the Ministry of Internal Affairs itself, that is, Mr. Zepinic, who is the deputy minister, and Mr. Mandic, who is an assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Mr. Zepinic is the gentleman who is referred to in the intercept as Vito or Vita?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As Vito, yes. Vito Zepinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn, then, to the next selected document, Mr. Treanor, which is found at tab 32 of binder 2. And this is a document dated 15 August 1991. Appears on your screen at the moment, Mr. Treanor, with only the date at the top, highlighted. Can you explain the significance of that document to the Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, this is getting down to some of the more day-to-day concerns of the SDS leadership. This document is a directive, if you will, from Dr. Karadzic, as the president of the SDS, to all the municipal and regional boards of the SDS, instructing them to introduce a system of coded communication as of the 1st of September. Maybe we could highlight what I have as paragraph 7. It doesn't appear -- I'm sorry. This is a different document. I thought we were skipping this document. This is an instruction on the operation of the local party organs and joining them to have meetings once a week and that type of thing. This again was issued by Dr. Karadzic, as president of the SDS, to all municipal boards of the SDS. And in paragraph 4, if we could magnify that, we can see the idea repeated, which we've seen before, that every member of a local board should be entrusted with maintaining contact with 10 to 20 Serbian homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is the same networking system that Dr. Karadzic referred to in the November 1990 Knin interview?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, going back that far, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, the next documents that you've selected are a series of intercepts in August of 1991, the first involving Mrs. Plavsic and Mr. Mladenovic, the second involving Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Karadzic, and the third involving Mrs. Plavsic and Mr. Karadzic. If we could turn to them in order. The first will be found at tab 8 in the intercepts binder, Your Honours, and is dated 22 August 1991. The clip you will hear begins at page 2 of the English translation. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a conversation with a gentleman apparently from Belgrade, who is visiting Sarajevo and Mrs. Plavsic is discussing his schedule there. The gentleman wants to see various people, including Mr. Zulfikarpasic, who I mentioned, and Mr. Krajisnik. There's a reference to the Belgrade Initiative, and Mrs. Plavsic is telling Mr. Mladenovic that, the way I understand it, if things don't go well from the point of view of that initiative and the whole of Bosnia remaining within Yugoslavia, then the Bosnian Serbs were determined to split off and settle that issue once and for all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we can turn, then, to the next intercept.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just make a comment at this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in relation to the way the Prosecution is using this witness to explain certain conversations. That in and of itself is actually quite an unusual course. But the point I would make -- for example, this last conversation, I don't think really required any explanation from the witness, and I do feel it's a sort of conversation that Your Honours could look at without the benefit of someone basically reiterating the conversation. If there's something to be added, then perhaps there's a need for that, but I just wonder if there's any point to basically reiterating the conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe there's nothing unusual or noteworthy about an expert explaining or identifying the materials upon which he has relied for his conclusions, placing them in context or identifying portions of those materials, however self-evident they may appear to anyone, that bear emphasis. In fact, I would think the contrary would be true. If Mr. Treanor was inclined to over-explain materials, I think that would raise an objection by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes some of the explanation becomes so apparent from the text, and of course it's not now for the first time that we hear certain aspects. So in general terms, I would say Mr. Treanor is already limiting himself, but certainly to that extent I would agree with Ms. Loukas, there's no need to repeat something that has been said. But at the same time, I notice that this is done now and then, but not to an extent that it really bothers us a lot. But perhaps, Mr. Treanor, keep in mind, and whenever you explain something, that what was said, we read it and we -- well, heard it, of course, in a language we do not understand, but we could follow it. We always can read it again in the transcript, and whatever additions you have to make, we'd like to hear them. Mr. Tieger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn, then, to the next intercept, intercept of 27 August 1991 [sic], involving Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does that conversation, Mr. Treanor, also reflect tensions and concerns about the Muslim-Serb negotiations and circumstances?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have two conversations of the 26th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, it appears on the -- on our screen as the next intercept of the 20th of August, but I -- it's in my mind that you said the 26th. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For better clarification, Your Honour, the English translation of this particular intercept can be found at tab 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's the 26th of August, as far as I can see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for Mr. Treanor's benefit, if it is of assistance, the ERN on that intercept is 0305-5109.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not assisting much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the B/C/S ERN is 02079135.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The question was whether or not that conversation also reflected tensions between the Bosnian Serbs and the Muslims, but perhaps it's best to play the intercept and have your comments after it's been heard. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will only add there as a bit of context that of course the SDS leadership in BH was supporting the JNA in its military operations against Croatia, and I think reference is being made to that situation. The other authorities in BH, the SDA and the HDZ, of course, were not particularly supportive in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Loukas. Perhaps we have --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It's just in relation to that the last question and answer. "I think." I mean, there is a lot of speculation in that, and I mean it's one thing to have an expert witness commenting on tapes. But it just seems to me that we are opening the door somewhat to speculation here, and I think the witness should be careful in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, I do agree that we always should care not to speculate, but if there's any part on which you think it's rather speculation than any knowledge, I think it would be proper to ask the witness then, perhaps in cross-examination, what made him interpret the intercepts as he did, and then to find out to what extent it is speculation, to what extent he has good reasons for these interpretations. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. But the Chamber is certainly aware that the risk of -- you know, famous authors sometimes are surprised to see what other people read in their texts. But I'd rather leave it to cross-examination. But awareness is there, and if you say at a certain moment this cannot be anything else than asking for speculation, then of course you can object against the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask first a different thing. That is, could the text be scrolled back to the beginning? Is that possible? I do not need necessarily to hear the sound, but ... [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just -- my eyes are getting better and better, I think, because on that screen, as we see it now, there seems to be 27 of August. Krajisnik and Karadzic. So that's one day of difference. But it's not easy to see, I must say. Is there any explanation for that, or is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can check to see if it's anything other than a coding error, and of course get back to the Court if it is a matter of substance, rather than a simple discrepancy which should be modified in accordance with the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know what that date stands for. Perhaps it's the date on which they started working out or when they -- well, whatever it is. But I see that we are dealing with a transcript of a telephone conversation which is dated 26th, whereas 27th of August also appears on our screen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Mr. Treanor, before we leave that intercept, that portion of the intercept, can you tell us what the reference to parliament being finished refers to.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reference there is to the -- what I've been called the Assembly of BH, in which we have seen there was quite a bit of tension among the ruling parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could move, then, to the second clip, which is found at page 2 of the English translation. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, your comments, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a continued reflection of Mr. Krajisnik's concern about the situation within the Assembly, and there's also a reference to SUP, that is, the Secretariat of Internal Affairs, which at this time was in fact -- had recently been renamed as the Ministry of Internal Affairs, which was a matter of concern, I think we've mention it had before, to the SDS leaders, that is, the internal affairs within that ministry. So there are some problems there that he would like to discuss as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There's further reference to letting others expose against the army and thereby marginalise themselves. What is that a reference to?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, apparently the state of relations between the -- among the three parties is such that Dr. Karadzic believes that the other two parties are trying to push the SDS out of the picture, so to speak, in their effort, among other things, to oppose -- the other two parties oppose the JNA and the military operations going on in Croatia. But he believes that they may succeed in only marginalising themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn, then, to the next intercept, which is found at tab 10, the conversation involving Mrs. Plavsic and Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this first clip begins at page 2 of the English translation. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, what is the concern being expressed here?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here again we see a reflection of the negotiations that are going on and Dr. Karadzic's concerns with how they're going or may not be going, and what he plans to do if -- may be planning to do if they in fact break down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could then turn to tab 33 of binder 2. And this is a handwritten letter addressed to President Karadzic personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we see on screen two section that is are highlighted. For the record, the first is the sentence that appears at number 1, and the second is the sentence that appears at number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, just for our own orientation: Should I conclude from the signature, which says "a signature," that it's unknown who wrote this letter or is there -- you said this is a letter to Dr. Karadzic, but from whom, or is that still to be established?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll wait and see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And let's address that question first, Mr. Treanor. Who is the author of this letter?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this report was written by Velibor Ostojic, who was a prominent member of the SDS and was the minister of information in the BH government. It relates to some meetings he had in Belgrade on the 3rd, and I believe the 4th, of September, with officials of the government of the Republic of Serbia, including the prime minister of Serbia, the minister of information of Serbia, and the minister for relations with Serbs, outside of Serbia, and he also had contacts with officials in the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia, including a meeting with one of the under-secretaries and spoke by telephone with the minister himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted certain sections of this report. If we could turn first to the highlighted sections in the first page. I've already indicated their placement within that document for the record, so you need not read them out verbatim, but if you would comment on them, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these two highlighted portions express the desire of the SDS leadership to have more military equipment at their disposal, as well as communications equipment, particularly with a view to apparently setting up their own television station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in the next highlighted clip, which is found at page 3 of the English translation, does Mr. Ostojic express a more general suggestion about the approach to be taken by the SDS?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the end he makes some recommendations to Dr. Karadzic. In paragraph 11, he states that: "In addition to public political activity the following should be formed and given assignments: A group responsible for defence, a group responsible for internal affairs, a group responsible for the economy, a group responsible for information, and that activity should be conducted on two levels: Public political activity and undercover work performed by assigned persons."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, as tensions mounted between the Bosnian Serbs and the Bosnian Muslims, did Bosnian Serb leaders consider warning Muslim leaders of the consequences if an agreement wasn't reached? And if that respect, can I ask you to turn to the intercept located at tab 11 between Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Karadzic of September 4, 1991. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, what aspects of the ongoing situation or relations between Bosnian Serbs and Bosnian Muslims or between the leaders of the Bosnian Serbs was reflected in that intercept?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think we see reflected here Dr. Karadzic's increasing frustration with the situation. I think probably within the context of the negotiations, the talks, at least, that were going on, and then a particular incident in which some Muslims were killed by Serbs, and he suggests that Mr. Izetbegovic be made aware of the fact that this is where Mr. Izetbegovic's policy was leading to this type of tension and to those types of consequences for the Muslim people. There are references to various individuals in here that we met before. Again, Vito is Vito Zepinic, and further on we see more discussion of the situation within the Ministry of Internal Affairs that Mr. Krajisnik is attempting to deal with, with -- in consultation with Mr. Mandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the second segment of this intercept to be played can be found on page 3 of the English translation. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, where is Mr. Krajisnik making selections and who is being sent down to Drvar?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here Mr. Krajisnik has been made aware of some political problems in Drvar on the -- within the Executive Committee of that municipality, and he's suggesting sending Rajko, who I presume is -- would be Rajko Dukic, who is chairman -- the president of the SDS Executive Committee down there to see what's going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Any other comments before we move on to the third segment of that intercept?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could comment that Mr. Cancar, who is referred to, is presumably Petko Cancar, who is an SDS Deputy in the Assembly and in fact the president of the Chamber of Municipalities of the Assembly. I'm not sure who Milos is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the final segment from that intercept, Your Honours, is also found on page 3 of the English translation. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, this aspect of the intercept appears to move on to a focus on Prijedor municipality and then back to a concern about what will Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. happen in two hours, a return to the original segment of the intercept. Can you tell us what aspect of the organisational structure or interrelations of SDS members are reflected in that intercept.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This discussion seems to relate to local problems in the party in Prijedor, the Srdjo being referred to is Srdjo Srdic who is an SDS deputy in the Assembly of BH from Prijedor. And then at the end they refer to having a meeting or something of that nature in two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at tab 12 of the intercept binder we can find the next intercept to be played, and the participants in that telephone conversation are Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before we begin the intercept, Mr. Treanor, I note that the date that appears on the English translation is 20 December. Can you tell us whether that appears to be an accurate date or not.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume we're referring to the conversation, the transcript of which bears the ERN 02066246.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This conversation, judging on the internal evidence, that is, things that are mentioned within the conversation, took place on the 6th of September. For instance, there's a reference to The Hague Conference beginning the next day, which occurred on the 7th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And with that clarification, if we could begin the first segment of the intercept, which is found at page 2 of the English translation. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you've already mentioned the commencement of The Hague Conference on September 7th. Can you amplify other aspects of that intercept.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we see a reflection here of what the Serbian position there is, and reference again to the situation in Krajina where Dr. Karadzic is trying to keep the leaders in Bosnian Krajina in line. Apparently the idea of uniting Bosnian Krajina with Croatian Krajina has crept up again at what he believes at - and Mr. Milosevic seems to agree - a very inopportune moment, in view of the ongoing negotiations. That's all the talk about the need for discipline and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could move to the second segment of that conversation, which appears on page 3 of the English translation. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here we see a reference again to the Belgrade Initiative, which I discussed earlier. This is -- Mr. Milosevic is saying that this is still alive and he will be using this in the negotiations. There's also -- I would call attention to the portion where Dr. Karadzic refers to as the -- his discussions with Mr. Izetbegovic, and his belief that they have come to an agreement that one side will not impose its views on the other. As we've been discussing here over the last couple of days, one of the great fears of the SDS leadership was of -- was of just that, of the fear of outvoting, as they frequently put it, where the two other parties would line up against them in the Assembly and simply outvote them on the -- in particular, the main issue of the day, which was the status of BH within Yugoslavia. At this point, Dr. Karadzic believes that he has an agreement with Mr. Izetbegovic that that will not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next intercept is found at tab 13, and the portion of the intercept that will be played is found at page 3 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I'm just first trying to verify a matter. I remember, but perhaps we could read it. Part of this English text, there was a part which was not written out, and I tried to compare what I've received now on paper, and it was about the top --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that was the fact that -- I noticed that as we were going through too. They missed out the word "opt for," that phrase, "opt for."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Or I --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's what it sounded like to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Certain moment where it was something that was not written down. I thought what I understood was "conceived by" or something. But I wonder whether we -- what we have got in front of us as the transcript is exactly the same as what we read on the screen, Mr. Tieger. And the only place where we can check it is the English text, as a matter of fact, and of course it --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, Your Honour, of course it was our intention to ensure that the text in front of you was the same as the text that was synchronised with the intercept and shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it possible to have on the screen again, especially the -- I would say the English part of the text spoken by the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. person with the initial "S"? [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There, for example, we see already a difference, where in the text it appears that they say "opt for" and it doesn't appear in the -- that's not the only difference, I'm afraid. What is in the next dot: "Although --" and then: "Top representatives." I thought I understood: "Although conceived by." But could we hear that specific part again. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There again, Mr. -- the text on the tape says: "Although conceived by top representatives." This is expressed by three dots and what we see on the screen, and it disappears on the written text.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there may be two separate concerns, if I'm hearing the Court correctly. The portion of the transcript which the Court just referred appears to be the same in the translation I have before me as on the screen, although I can hear the same words the Court can hear in English as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I do not see any dots appearing, so there's no indication of missing words in the English text as we received it on paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would indicate, we are having -- we have the similar issue that you've identified. The text of what appears on the monitor and the text of what appears on the hard copy, there are differences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I can imagine that we can't solve it right away, and of course what is of some concern to me is that these are a few words spoken in English where we have an opportunity to verify, whereas all the other words, I can't read the B/C/S version and see whether it's complete, I cannot check any translation. But I notice that this at least is not fully congruent, and you're invited, although it's an annex to the expert's report, but the expert can be invited or the Prosecution can take care that we receive congruent versions of what we see on the screen and what we have on paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll certainly do our best to ensure that that happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's for this moment, because we could -- we can't solve the whole of the problem right now, but please proceed, Mr. -- I think you wanted to -- you wanted to ask the witness something about the next intercept.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, we were about to move on to an intercept which is found at tab 13, as I indicated to the Chamber earlier, the segment that will be played is found at page 3 of the English translation. And this is another conversation between Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Milosevic. And first of all, before we begin: I understand that there were a number of intercepts that were inexplicably -- bore the date of 20 December [sic] as the previous one and that have been identified by date on the basis of context. You explained the previous intercept as being dated on September 6th, through the reasons you described, and I understand that this intercept is dated 9 September. Is that correct? And if so, can you explain that to the Court.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The context -- I'm sorry. Not the context. The content of this intercept would indicate that it took place in September, on or about the 9th of September. It refers to two meetings, one to take place on Thursday, and the other on Friday. The Thursday meeting was to take place in Strasbourg, and the Friday meeting in Belgrade, again, a meeting to do with the Belgrade Initiative. So it seems to have taken place a few days before those meetings. The Thursday was the 12th of September, and then Friday was the 13th of September. I believe there is some other evidence which -- in the form of the original operator's notes in relation to this intercept, which give it a date of the 9th, but the exact date is not certain. But, as I say, very close to these two meetings which are referred to in the conversation as planning for these meetings, which Mr. Milosevic is very interested in. In fact, the meeting in -- or the event in Strasbourg that he wanted Mr. Krajisnik to go to took place on the 13th, on the Friday, rather than on the Thursday, and the meeting in Belgrade, for the Belgrade Initiative, which was a big meeting of representatives from the three republics that I mentioned earlier, that is, Serbia, Montenegro, and BH, took place in Belgrade on Monday, the 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You make reference to a meeting in Strasbourg. Do you do that on the basis of the original text? Because both in the B/C/S version of the transcript and in the English, it's not Strasbourg, but it's perhaps a bit surprising. It's Salzburg.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, reference is made to the European Parliament. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At one place is says Salzburg, as the seat of the European Parliament. So I read that as Strasbourg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm aware of that. You are talking about Strasbourg, but I read Salzburg.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both versions, of course in the translation it's -- did you check in the original whether -- or is this part of the portion to be played?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't believe the beginning of this is going to be played. However, toward the end -- yes. In the end, the clip, the second clip we will be hearing, it says Strasbourg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. We'll then hear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Excuse me. In view of the time, perhaps it's best if we forego playing the intercept until after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do agree with you. We will take a break of 20 minutes. We'll reconvene at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we were about to hear a new text. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the Court would like me to quickly address the translation issues you raised earlier, I can defer it for another time, if it's more appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could hear already your explanation and see whether it is in need of any further debate or discussion. Please tell us, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I have verified that the document that was synchronised is indeed the same document that appears in the text -- or in the copies the Court has. Secondly, the reference to Salzburg that appears in the early part of the translation, both English and B/C/S, I had wondered whether one of the participants misspoke or whether it was a typo or misheard by the person who transcribed it. It appears to be the latter. On the intercept itself, I'm told you can clearly hear "Strasbourg."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said that the document we received on paper is the same as the transcribed. But as far as the dots are concerned, "conceived by," or "opt for," it certain is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No. That's correct. I think the explanation for that, Your Honour, is in the -- and I'll verify that. I believe it's the effort to ensure that the synchronisation is accurate, and where a word is not heard or does not appear, I think they use the ellipses to extend the portion to do that. Now in that connection, I would mention one further thing. As the Court is aware, during the course of this predominantly B/C/S conversation, some English is used. That English was translated into B/C/S in the transcription of the document, so that the entire B/C/S document is in that language, both, obviously, the portions that were spoken in B/C/S and the English portions. And that -- then there's an English translation of that B/C/S portion. So there is -- that accounts for the discrepancy between the words the Court heard when listening to the speaker in English, and the English translation itself. In other words, the English translation is an attempt to accurately translate the B/C/S transcript, the B/C/S written transcript, rather than go back and forth between the transcript that was provided to the translator and the original intercept itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That, it seems to me, is a relatively unique circumstance in the context of these intercepts, which I don't suspect will -- it is likely to surface frequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say the risk of further mistakes is small because this is very specific situation where English is spoken by the participants in the conversation, who usually speak B/C/S. Yes. Yes, I do understand that. Nevertheless, you're still invited to provide the Chamber with a copy with -- well, how to do it? If it's a translation of the original, then I take it that the dots will reappear. At the same time, I think we have now heard at least two of the dots explained by the original English text, that is, "opted for" and "conceived by." We'll wait and see, but thank you for your explanation up to this moment, Mr. Tieger. I wonder whether the Defence would make any further submissions in respect of this explanation and what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Not in relation to that. I have no further observations to make, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I think we can now play the intercept itself. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, that was a short clip after a long preface, but perhaps you can assist us with that.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the only commentary necessary here is that at the beginning of the clip, the "they" who's being referred to are, of course, the coalition partners of the SDS. I think in this case in particular, the SDA. I don't know who Vlado is. And we didn't get to the part which I thought we were going to hear, the next sentence or so, where Strasbourg was in fact mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If the Chamber could then turn to tab 34 of binder 2, we can move on to the next document, which is a 12 September meeting of SDS government members. And if we could display the first highlighted portion on screen. Your Honour, that first portion can be found on page 3 of your copies. And for the record, the portion highlighted is that which reads: "Record of a meeting of the officials," down to SDS BiH members, and then the first sentence that appears thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, can you tell us the nature of this meeting.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a meeting of one of the groups of officials that I have mentioned before, that is, the SDS-designated members of the government of BH and other high-level officials in the various ministries and institutions within that government's -- below the ministerial level, and they are meeting on this occasion to discuss their common concerns as representatives of their party in those institutions and some of their dissatisfaction with the way things are going emerge in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next highlight, which appears at page 7 of the English translation. And for the record, that highlight appears at number 11 of the enumerated paragraphs and begins: "To propose the setting up of a duty system."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just to expand a little more. The dissatisfaction expressed at this meeting has as much to do with the type of cooperation between the parties on internal government personnel and other matters as anything else, and they perceive the need to keep in better touch with each other and with the SDS leadership. So therefore, we see in this paragraph their recommendation to set up a duty system in order to monitor activities for the implementation of tasks in state organs, day-to-day problem management in different fields and to serve as a liaison with the SDS. With this in mind, Ljubisav Terzic, in the original, and Dragan Kapetina were tasked with developing a method of communication of the SDS and cadres or personnel of the SDS in republic state organs, in the republican state organs with the municipalities. Terzic and Kapetina are two of the SDS officials I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does the document also reflect who the record of this meeting of top-level SDS government functionaries was sent?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As we can see, it was sent to Dr. Karadzic, Mr. Krajisnik, and Mrs. Plavsic and Dr. Koljevic, who were members of the Presidency, of course. Mr. Cancar, who I mentioned earlier today, who was the president of the Chamber of Municipalities in Assembly and an SDS member, and Rajko Dukic, who was the president of the Executive Committee of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to the duty system that was suggested by these high-level SDS government functionaries, was there a growing interest in the summer of 1991 in the SDS in the development of some form of covert intelligence or information-gathering and exchange system?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of documents we have, that would certainly seem to be the case, and especially when taken in conjunction with the document we just examined, which recommends certain steps in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to a series of documents, the first of which begins at tab 35 of binder 2. That document now appears on screen, and the cover page, a portion of which is highlighted, indicates: "Strictly confidential, the intelligence and security system of the Serbian Democratic Party instructions."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it bears, at the top of the page, under the heading, "Serbian Democratic Party of BH," the title of the National Security Council, which is a body within the SDS, about which we otherwise know very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could move quickly to these documents. First I'd like to go to the highlighted portion which appears on page 3 of the English translation and now appears on screen. This is a diagram of the proposed system that accompanied the document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. As you can see, it's a little bit complex, but the main idea here is the inclusion of the various circles of officials on various levels that are available to the SDS leadership to draw on as far as gaining information on the other hand, and carrying out Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. instructions, on the other, is concerned. The headed at the top by the Main Board with the National Security Council -- the Security Council reporting to it and drawing information from the different republican and municipal-level institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Next document is found at tab 36. It currently appears on screen, and the highlighted portion says: "Instructions," and then immediately below it: "Regarding the organisation of officials and high-ranking government officers, duty roster and coordination with SDS duty officers."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does that document appear to have anything to do with the recommendation for the establishment of a watch system?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This seems to be a reflection of the recommendations which we saw in the document about the meeting of the SDS government functionaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could move to tab 37, please. This document which now appears on screen bears no highlights but is headed: "Communication system - code."

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an elementary code system which comes from the records of the SDS, with simple code designations for the various leaders, and then for other individuals, probably the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And as shown on that document the first two names --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the bodyguards or other escorts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the second clip --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we move on to that, I'm just wondering if there's any indication of dates in relation to that last document, under tab 37 that we were looking at. And also, I think, in relation to 36 there doesn't appear to be a date as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure if that's an objection or the beginning of a premature cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think Ms. Loukas would like to know whether there's any date attached to it so that could prevent her perhaps from asking any questions about it. We get a lot of explanation on documents, and where I also asked a few times, is the sender known, is the date known? I thought this is trying to assist the Chamber to better understand the document. Could you please indicate whether dates are known for these documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, obviously, the documents themselves bear no dates, and I am only able to place them in conjunction, as I mentioned, in conjunction with at least one other document which we've seen, that is, the meeting of the high-level functionaries, which mentions a system similar to one that is portrayed in the instructions. Other than that, at this point in time, I can't give any date to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No date. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move to tab 38, please, in binder 2, and turn to a document now on screen, the upper portion of which is highlighted and says: "Serbian Democratic Party of BH, strictly confidential." Below that: "President, number, Sarajevo, August 1991." And finally: "To all municipal and regional boards of SDS of BH."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The nature of that document, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document I thought we were referring to at the beginning of today's session. This is an instruction from Dr. Karadzic, as president of the SDS to the boards mentioned, instructing them to introduce a code system as of the 1st of September, 1991. And I would draw attention in particular to paragraph 7. If we don't have that, I could just read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No. It's on screen now.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There we are. "For communication between the municipality and the Main Board, and for mutual communication, use the telephone code that we gave you as frequently as possible." So here again we see another reference, or a reference to codes now. Now is the particular code that's being referred to, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, on Friday, we discussed the commencement of regionalisation as reflected in the establishment of the Community of Municipalities, as well as the reaction to the establishment of that -- of those institutions. As we move now into September of 1991, was there a further push or effort toward regionalisation by the SDS?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. As I mentioned earlier, there was, on the one hand, a certain desire among circles in the SDS to forge ahead with regionalisation; on the other hand, there was the need to -- for some caution, in view of discussions that were going on with the Bosnian Muslim political parties who were not too keen on this project, with Dr. Karadzic urging patience in the matter to his SDS subordinates. For whatever reason, in September, in early September, the SDS leadership decided to proceed with the development of regionalisation, as we will see in -- from coming documents. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at tab 39, the 25 September decision on appointing staff for regionalisation, that document appears in the English translation, and it is shown on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, you've highlighted both the date of that decision, as well as the paragraph headed "number 2," toward the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The document we're looking at bears the date of 25 September, but the important event here is mentioned in the paragraph 2, which is highlighted. There was a meeting on the 7th of September, one of the high-level SDS meetings with various officials present. Dr. Karadzic referred to this meeting as upcoming the next day in the conversation of the 6th of September with Mr. Milosevic, and we read now in paragraph 2 in this document of the city board of the -- City Board of Sarajevo of the SDS that -- which relates to the creation of a regionalisation staff within that particular organisation, that: "The staff shall coordinate the implementation of the decision and of the conclusions adopted at the Pale symposium of municipal, regional, and republic SDS organs of 7 September 1991 for the region: City of Sarajevo, together with the staff of the BH, SDS Main Board for regional organisation in all SDS municipal boards." So the meeting of 7 September 1991 seems to have been key for the further development of the regionalisation process by the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we turn, then, to a September 16th meeting of the Executive Board, which may be found at tab 40 of the binder 2. The first highlighted portion of that document indicates: "Minutes of the third meeting of the Executive Board of the Serbian Democratic Party of BH, held on the 16th of September, 1991." And if we could turn to the next highlighted portion, please. That appears at the top of page 2 of the English translation, under item 1.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see reference made to the regionalisation staff formed at the centre of the SDS: "Decision on the appointment of the regionalisation staff was considered and adopted in accordance with the conclusion adopted at the consultations in Pale. The decision and the statement of reasons were forwarded to the municipal boards and the town board or the city board of the SDS. During the discussion it was asserted that the criterion for the choice of people composing the staff was good." So here we have another concrete result of that meeting, that is, the formation of the regionalisation staff of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I referred earlier to the foundation or establishment of the Community of Municipalities in April of 1991. Was there a transformation of the Community of Municipalities in September of 1991, consistent with the movement toward further regionalisation?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what we see at this time, and I would emphasise that we do not know the content of the discussions or the decisions that were reached at the 7 September meeting, but what we see at this time is the, meeting in September, the creation of a number of so-called Serbian Autonomous Districts. At least three of these districts were formed from previously existing communities of municipalities. Earlier we discussed, in particular, the Community of Municipalities of Bosnian Krajina, which was established on the 25th of April, at a meeting in Celinac. In May, communities of municipalities were also formed in Eastern Herzegovina and in the Romanian region, which is in the mountains east of Sarajevo. In the middle of September, we see those three communities of municipalities proclaimed as being now Serbian Autonomous Regions. At that time, a fourth Serbian Autonomous -- I'm sorry, Serbian Autonomous Districts. A fourth Serbian Autonomous District was also formed, that is, in the middle of September, and by the beginning of November, two additional Serbian Autonomous Districts were formed. There is some confusion in the terminology here, since the Community of Municipalities of Bosnian Krajina transformed itself, if you will, into the Autonomous Region of Krajina, using the word "region" rather district. They did this presumably to avoid confusion with the already existing Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina, which was in fact in Croatia and centred in Knin. We had an earlier document in which Dr. Karadzic congratulated the leaders in Knin on the establishment of that particular entity. That entity had a background similar to at least three of the Serbian Autonomous Districts in Bosnian that I'm referring to, that is, a Community of Municipalities of Northern Dalmatia and Lika was formed in June 1990, and that transformed itself into the Serbian Autonomous District of Krajina in December 1990. Now we're seeing the same development in Bosnia, where the communities of municipalities are transforming themselves into what we call generically Serbian Autonomous Districts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have one binder that has not been marked for identification, that is, the maps and charts binder. I'd like to have that marked at this time. And then put before the Court one of the maps from that binder. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The binder will be Prosecution Exhibit number P68.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the map currently on screen can be found at tab 13 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if you look at your screen, can you tell us what that depicts, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. We may be jumping ahead of ourselves a little bit here. This map is based on information as of the 21st of November, 1991, as you'll see in the lower left, in the legend. At that time, the Serbian Autonomous Districts were composed of certain territories which -- or claimed to be composed of certain territories which were basically of three types, and I think we'll see a document on this later on. The territories in dark blue are municipalities -- what we have depicted here are municipalities with the names on the map are the names of municipalities. The ones in dark blue are municipalities which, as a whole, belonged to Serbian Autonomous Districts. The ones in light blue are municipalities in which certain Serbian areas within those municipalities declared their adhesion to the Serbian autonomous districts. That is, in a manner of speaking, the municipalities were divided. These are municipalities which the SDS did not control, as opposed to the ones in blue, which, in principle, are ones that were under SDS political control. The document on which this is -- this map is based on also refers to other territories that could belong to the autonomous -- Serbian autonomous districts, which it defined in rather vague terms, for instance, areas which had been -- in which the Serbs had been in a majority until the genocide during World War II, that sort of thing. So it's impossible for us to depict that on these maps. But this is the closest depiction we can come to on a map of the territories of the Serbian autonomous districts. As I say, the process began of establishing districts as opposed to the communities of municipalities in the middle of September and continued through early November, and this depicts the situation as of 21 November 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger. The legend is not very clear to me, Mr. Treanor. The first is a box, wide, with a dark black line, black square.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Your Honour. The reference there I think is being made to the dark black line around the box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So the dark black line that you'll see on the map shows the boundaries of the various Serbian autonomous districts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true that the white areas, for example, in the centre of Bosnia-Herzegovina, is also surrounded by a black line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The white areas are those municipalities which are not in either all or in part in the fashion I described, included within the districts. If you see one surrounded by a black line, that's simply because it abuts on two different SAOs and is therefore surrounded by SAOs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or the coast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or the coast, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I look at the centre, the centre, the white centre --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map section, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- is completely surrounded by thick black lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. That would be the external boundary of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the south, if you will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And in the interior, that would show the furthest extent of the Serbian autonomous districts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's not a very clear way of defining your legends, but thank you for your explanation. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could return, then, to mid-September and the transformation of the Community of Municipalities in the Krajina, and turn specifically to the September 16th decision on proclamation of the Autonomous Region of the Krajina, found at tab 41 of binder 2. The document currently on screen has a number of sections highlighted, including the decision on the proclamation, Articles 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if you could explain the significance of those highlights, Mr. Treanor, please.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, let me say that again we're showing documents relating to the Bosnian Krajina because that is the area which we do have most documentation from. We know of the existence of the other Serbian Autonomous Districts through other means, which are mentioned in our report in the appropriate section. So here, if we could magnify Article 1. This refers to the alliance, that is, what we've been calling Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the community of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina, "Declared the Autonomous Region of Krajina an autonomous democratic unit of sovereign citizens and peoples and an inseparable part of the federative Yugoslavia as a federal state, which consists of the republics of Serbia and Montenegro and the other federal units, which have expressed their free will to remain in this state." This document being dated, as I think was mentioned, the 16th of September, on which at this session of the Assembly of the autonomous -- of the municipal -- I'm sorry, the Community of Municipalities of Bosnian Krajina, the Assembly voted to transform it into this new autonomous region or Autonomous District of Krajina. And I think we can take a look at Article 2. "The territory of the region consists of Municipal Assemblies which joined the Alliance, that is, the Community of Municipalities, as well as villages, districts, and areas which will join later, in accordance with this decision."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This Article -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I think we can take a look at Article 3 as well, which states that: "Federal law, regulations, and other general legislation, laws, and regional legislation shall be applied on the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, as well as the legislation of BH, which is not incompatible with this legislation. Until the regional laws, regulations, and other legislation are passed, the laws, regulations, and legislation of the region, as well as the legislation of BH, shall be valid unless they are contrary to the constitution of the SFRY." In other words, the laws, regulations, and other legislation of the Federal State of Yugoslavia. So here we see a very strong link between these -- this autonomous region, certainly, and the Federal State of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you've also highlighted a portion that's found on page 2, that is, Article 7?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This states that: "The Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina will, in accordance with Article 265, paragraph 4 of the constitution of the Socialist Republic of BH, enable populated settlements from one municipality to be joined to another municipality, in accordance with the citizens' wish to do so." This is a reflection of one of the grievances of the SDS that I mentioned very early on, that is, the manner in which the boundaries of municipalities had been drawn in BH, as they felt to the detriment of the Serbs in BH. This Article providing that some changes be made in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, you've used the term "transformation" in connection with the change from a community of municipalities to an autonomous region. If we could look quickly at the statute of the Autonomous Region of the Krajina. Does that indicate the nature of the transformation which took place?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Your Honours, that document is found at tab 42.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, interestingly, the change that was made on the surface is mostly in regard to the name, the statute that was adopted and that here bears the date of the 16th of September is virtually identical to the statute of the Community of Municipalities of Bosnian Krajina. One change that does take place is of course changing the name of the entity from the old name to the new name, that is, Autonomous Region of Krajina. There are a couple of other minor differences. But the -- other than that, the statute is virtually the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if we could next turn to a letter dated September 16th, 1991. It is found at tab 43. The document on screen bears two highlights. One is the first paragraph, which appears under the heading: "Letter of support to the federal secretary of National Defence, general of the army, Veljko Kadijevic." And the other is the last paragraph of the letter, which appears immediately above the names of the signatories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we have no signal on our screens at this moment, so we have difficulties in following you. Yes. Yes, we are all on line again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, if you can tell us why you selected this document and its significance.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is reflective of two things in particular that I'd like to point out. One is the continued support for the Yugoslav People's Army, the JNA. As the Court will remember, that figured very early on in the programme of the SDS and continues during this period of hostilities in Croatia. I think we've alluded earlier to assistance in mobilisation and that sort of thing. And the -- by the SDS and, on the other hand, the opposition or reluctance of the other two parties in the governing coalition, the SDA and the HDZ, to support those military operations. And we also see reflected here the fear of outvoting, which is another Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. long-standing point in the SDS concerns. We see the first paragraph reading: "The decisions being passed by the organs of Bosnia and Herzegovina, especially by the government and the Presidency, relating to a unified system of defence of the country, are being passed by outvoting the legitimate representatives of the Serbian people in these bodies." These are decisions affecting -- referring to decisions which related to the call-up of reserves within Bosnia and which the other two parties did not want to participate in, on the one hand, and as I said, the SDS supporting that. So they're letting the army know that they are against decisions which are preventing complete mobilisation in BH. And then the last paragraph: "Therefore, in the name of the Serbian people and all the peaceful citizens of BH, we hereby fully support the unified armed forces of Yugoslavia in the execution of their constitutionally defined role and tasks."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we turn now to an intercept, a conversation between Mr. Karadzic and Mrs. Plavsic on 19 September, which can be found at tab 14 of the intercept binder.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I have a conversation on the 17th of September, ERN 02078969.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I may have misspoken. That is the document to which I was referring.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The screen does say 19 September. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And we'll turn to the second clip, which can be found at page 2 of the translation, unless you have some quick comments first.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'd just like to point out that Nedjo Vlaski was a member of the State Security Service and a Serb. The State Security Service is one of the two halves, if you will, of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the other the public, that is, basically the uniformed police. The concern is about his situation, and this is again a reflection as we've seen other things, of the tension between the SDS and its coalition partners over internal affairs within the Ministry of Internal Affairs, especially questions of personnel. [Intercept played] (no translation)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Part of the discontent of the SDS is reflected here, that is, that even though certain officials within MUP, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, were Serbs, they were not SDS Serbs, if you will, and what they want, of course, is their own people in the places they feel they are entitled to under the inter-party agreement. You also see reflected Dr. Karadzic's belief that the way they're being treated in this regard is the type of thing that will happen to them in general if BH should become independent and the Bosnian Serbs are left in that state as a minority. And then we see reference now to a strategy to deal with that situation, that is, if we're not getting what we believe we should get according to the inter-party agreement, then perhaps what we should do is split the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we turn now to a document of September 21, 1991. That document can be found at tab 44, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I perhaps first ask a clarification on the last intercept. You told us, Mr. Treanor, that: "Part of the discontent of the SDS is reflected here, that is, that even though certain officials within MUP were Serbs, they were not SDS Serbs, if you will, and what they want, of course, is their own people in the place they feel they are entitled to, under the inter-party agreement." Could you indicate a bit more in detail where you read this in the intercept, especially the distinction between non-SDS Serbs and the wish to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I'm providing a bit of background here, but right at the beginning of that clip, Dr. Karadzic says: "As long as they don't appoint in SUP, that is, exactly until they stop determining where, what Serb will work." Then Mrs. Plavsic says: "Yes, exactly. As long as they don't stop determining. So he's not happy with the way even Serbs are being appointed. And we do have a lot of other information on this subject, but here is reflected the concern that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That the SDS was not getting to determine which Serbs would work where.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you read that in: "Until in SUP it appoints, I mean, until they stop deciding where shall each individual Serb work?" Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I would render that as where which Serb will work. So it's a selection of -- selecting people and the place that they will work. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can't say that it's yet crystal clear, but we are in the beginning of this trial. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
